## What is dispatched, and what is deliberately NOT

⭐ **The card names its own first deliverable and this claim does not widen it**, verbatim: 「本卡的第一件事是**把矛盾定死**,不是修。」

⇒ **Pin the contradiction. ⛔ Do not fix anything, ⛔ do not open a PR, ⛔ do not edit `ci.yml`, `turbo.json` or any cache config.** Two readings disagree and at least one of them is about a mechanism nobody has named yet; naming which side is wrong *is* the deliverable.

⚠️ This seat cannot arm a PR touching `.github/workflows/**` (`auto_merge` answers 422 every time), so a fix landing there is a human merge and a separate decision. That is a second reason this flight is read-only, not the first one — the first is the card's own sentence.

## The contradiction, as the card states it

⏱️ The two rows below are **quoted from the card**, which states its own reading time: 2026-09-17T13:41Z. ⛔ This seat has re-measured neither of them — that is the flight's first job.

| half | reading | status on the card |
|---|---|---|
| the graph | a diff touching only `packages/spec/src/**` pulls `@objectstack/cli` into the affected set | **MEASURED** by the filing seat, with a control |
| that run | quoted from the card, whose own reading time is 2026-09-17T13:41Z — CI run `34746808828` (head `c7ae2c1026`) reports `cache-replayed packages, excluded as non-measurements: 1 (@objectstack/cli)`, every `@objectstack/cli` row marked `replayed log` ⇒ the task **never executed**, while all six shards reported success | **RELAYED** — ⛔ the filing seat did **not** re-measure it |

⇒ **Re-read that timing table yourself before anything else.** The card says so in as many words: 「立卡的人要先自己读回那张计时表再动手。」 Everything downstream rests on it.

⚠️ **How to read it, because the obvious route fails here**: `GET /actions/jobs/{id}/logs` redirects to blob storage and the container proxy answers **403**. The original dev got it through the MCP github tool. ⭐ **MCP github READ tools are permitted** (`mcp__github__get_job_logs`, `mcp__github__actions_get`, …) — it is only MCP **write** tools that are banned. Use the read tool for this leg and REST for everything else, and say in the report which channel answered.

## ⛔ The instrument discipline the card already paid for — inherit it, do not re-learn it

The filing seat recorded its own error, and it is the trap on this card:

> `turbo ls --affected` **不钉 `TURBO_SCM_BASE` 时,干净树也读回 76** —— 本席第一次就是这么读的,而 76 正是 dev 报回的那个数。⇒ **不钉 base 的 `--affected` 读数一律作废**

⭐ Note what that means: **76 is the number an unpinned reading returns on a clean tree**, and 76 is also the number the original dev reported as the affected-set size. ⇒ ⛔ Any `--affected` reading in your report that does not state its pinned `TURBO_SCM_BASE` is not a reading, and if you reproduce 76 you must show it came from a pinned base and not from the null case.

The card's own pinned readings, to reproduce rather than cite: clean tree ⇒ **0**; only `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` ⇒ **76** incl. `@objectstack/cli`; only `packages/types/src/env.ts` ⇒ **68**, also incl. `@objectstack/cli`.

## The two probes the card names — run both, report both

1. **`ci.yml`'s per-shard `actions/cache` `restore-keys`** — they fall back **across branches and across commits**. Read them and say exactly what a fallback hit would restore.
2. **Hash comparison**: the whole-package leg (`turbo run test test:repo` with its chain of `--filter`) versus the hash a local `--dry=json` plan computes. The card's table came from the latter; nobody has compared them.

## What "pinning the contradiction" has to produce

A verdict naming **which** of these is true, with the reading that settles it:

- **(A)** the affected-set reading is right and the task really was cache-replayed while genuinely affected ⇒ a live cache-correctness defect, and the card says ⭐ **re-grade to p1 immediately**;
- **(B)** the run's report is right and the task was not actually affected in *that* run's context (different base, different filter chain, different hash inputs) ⇒ the graph reading does not transfer, and say precisely why;
- **(C)** both readings are right about different objects ⇒ **name the mechanism that makes them different**, which is the thing the card says nobody has named.

⛔ "Probably a cache flake" is not a verdict. ⛔ Do not leave it at "needs more investigation" without naming what would settle it.

## Controls you owe

1. Every `--affected` reading states its pinned base, and the **clean-tree null case** is run in the same session so a number can be told apart from the unpinned artefact.
2. The timing-table re-read either **reproduces** the `cache-replayed … 1 (@objectstack/cli)` line verbatim or reports that it could not be read and by which channel it failed — ⛔ "could not read" is never "not there".
3. ⛔ **No zero without a control.** If you report that some cache key never falls back, show the same reading finding a fallback where one exists.

## ⛔ Out of scope

⛔ Any edit anywhere. ⛔ #10032 (a task that RAN but captured no output) — the card read it and calls it adjacent-but-not-twin, and folding them would make both unsayable. ⛔ Re-litigating #18236 / PR #18667, whose bare-specifier premise was already falsified (0 of 349 importer→imported pairs missing a manifest edge). ⛔ Re-grading this card — if the answer is (A), **say so and recommend p1**; the label write is the PM's.

## Deliverable

The verdict plus every reading and control, posted as a comment on this card, and the `os-dev-report` JSON returned to me. ⛔ No PR, ⛔ no branch push beyond what your tooling needs.

⛔ Commit trailer, if you make any commit, is **model-free**: `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` beside `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017ef78bLdybu3AffehKkhfk`. The repo's `.githooks/pre-push` refuses a model identifier there (measured this shift). No model identifier in anything pushed to the repository.
⛔ REST writes need `-H "Content-Type: application/json"`. MCP github **write** tools are banned; MCP github **read** tools are fine and are the intended channel for the job logs.

## Verdict: **(A)** — genuinely affected, and cache-replayed anyway. The defect is live, and the mechanism nobody had named is `--only`.

Both halves of the card are true readings, and they are true of **two different turbo invocations of the same task** in the same job. The graph half is right: a `packages/spec/src/**` diff pulls `@objectstack/cli` into the affected set (reproduced below, pinned, with the null control). The run half is right: `@objectstack/cli#test` never executed in run `34746808828`. They are not in conflict because CI does not run that task once — it runs the **whole-package leg** (`turbo run test test:repo` with a chain of `--filter`) for most packages and a **separate sliced leg** for a package the partitioner slices:

```
pnpm turbo run test "--filter=$PKG" --only --concurrency=4 --summarize --log-order=stream -- "--shard=$SLICE"
```

`--only` removes the dependency tasks from the run graph. Measured on this tree, that also removes them from the **hash**: the sliced leg's hash for `@objectstack/cli#test` no longer carries the `build` / `^build` chain, which is the only path by which a change in `packages/spec` reaches it. What survives is the package's own files plus the hand-declared `$TURBO_ROOT$` inputs in `turbo.json`. So the sliced leg can — and here did — hit a main-seeded cache entry across a spec change that the affected-set computation had just declared relevant.

⇒ Recommending **p1**, on the card's own condition: 「若探针复现出「受影响的任务仍被缓存重放」,⛔ 立即改判 p1。」 The label write is the PM's, not mine. ⛔ No fix is included here: the card's first deliverable is 「把矛盾定死」, and the fix lands in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which this seat cannot arm.

### 1. The timing table, re-read first-hand (REPRODUCED verbatim)

Channel: **MCP `get_job_logs`** on job `103697977573` (the aggregate `Test Core` job). REST `GET /actions/jobs/ID/logs` fails before it starts — the egress proxy denies CONNECT to the blob host (`curl: (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`).

```
- of those, read out of a turbo cache **replay**: **251** — true durations, measured by the run that filled the cache rather than by this one
- packages measured: **70**
- cache-replayed packages, excluded as non-measurements: **1** (`@objectstack/cli`)
```

and the row the card quotes:

```
| 18 | 29.51 | 12 | `test/scaffold-emission-typechecks.test.ts _(unit)_` | `@objectstack/cli` | replayed log |
```

The card's RELAYED half stands as written.

### 2. The run itself: which leg replayed, and whose log it replayed

Channel: **MCP `get_job_logs`** on job `103696221055` — `Test Core (5/6)` of run `34746808828`. End of its test step, verbatim:

```
@objectstack/cli:test:  Test Files  126 passed (126)
@objectstack/cli:test:       Tests  1789 passed (1789)
@objectstack/cli:test:    Start at  07:51:20
@objectstack/cli:test:    Duration  272.80s (transform 49.44s, setup 0ms, import 332.97s, tests 457.86s, environment 19ms)

  Tasks:    1 successful, 1 total
 Cached:    1 cached, 1 total
   Time:    73ms >>> FULL TURBO
```

Three facts fall out of those eight lines:

1. **`Tasks: 1 successful, 1 total`** — a one-task run. The whole-package leg schedules the `^build` closure with it (60 tasks for a `--filter=@objectstack/cli` plan on this tree, measured below). One task is the `--only` sliced leg and nothing else.
2. **`Cached: 1 cached, 1 total` / `73ms >>> FULL TURBO`** — the suite did not run. 1789 passing tests were printed out of a stored log.
3. **`Start at 07:51:20`**, while this job started at **08:06:09Z** (REST `/actions/runs/34746808828/jobs`). The log was produced ~15 minutes before the job that printed it existed. Only `push` runs on `main` save this cache (`Save Turbo cache (main only)`, `if: always() && github.event_name == 'push'`), and the only main push run whose `Test Core (5/6)` window contains `07:51:20` is run `34745708702` (head `bdb247d9ec`, pushed 07:37:55Z; its shard-5 job ran 07:38:16Z → 07:56:15Z). PR #17914 merged at 12:51Z that day, so the tree that produced this green cli suite could not contain the PR's `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` change.

That is the whole defect in one sentence: **the green `@objectstack/cli` suite reported by PR #17914's CI was computed on a `main` commit that did not contain PR #17914.**

### 3. The hash comparison (the card's probe 2) — the mechanism, measured

Worktree at `origin/main` `b7eaf6a61`, turbo **2.10.10** (same version CI ran), `--dry=json`, reading `tasks[].hash` for `@objectstack/cli#test`. Every mutation was transient, proven on disk (`git hash-object` against the `HEAD` blob) and restored (`git diff HEAD` empty afterwards); nothing was committed.

| tree | whole-package leg `turbo run test --filter=@objectstack/cli` | sliced leg `--only … -- --shard=1/2` |
|---|---|---|
| clean | `1a76a51a556c3aa0` (60 tasks) | `6c558a22d13a7916` (1 task) |
| PR #17914's **14 changed paths**, all mutated | `c2f62fc176c52f4b` — **moves** | `6c558a22d13a7916` — **identical** |
| only `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` | `fbdbe6359dfd2d8b` — **moves** | `6c558a22d13a7916` — **identical** |
| ⭐ control: `packages/cli/src/utils/one-shot-exit.ts` (inside the package) | `dfdde5540c2e0aa1` — **moves** | `4b226cb5977282a1` — **moves** |
| ⭐ control: `packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts` (a **declared** `$TURBO_ROOT$` input of `@objectstack/cli#test`) | — | `c16e8b1cf7fe4ace` — **moves** |

The two controls are what make the identical cells readable: the sliced-leg hash is not inert. It moves for a change inside the package, and it moves for a cross-package file that `turbo.json` names explicitly in that task's `inputs`. It does **not** move for anything reached only through the dependency graph.

Isolating which flag causes it:

| invocation | clean | after mutating `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` |
|---|---|---|
| plain | `1a76a51a556c3aa0` | `fbdbe6359dfd2d8b` — moves |
| plain + passthrough `-- --shard=1/2` | `7efd4d61743acf35` | `1c05e282572148e8` — moves |
| `--only` | `6b7e234fcba9c296` | `6b7e234fcba9c296` — **identical** |
| `--only` + passthrough | `6c558a22d13a7916` | `6c558a22d13a7916` — **identical** |

⇒ It is **`--only`**, not the `--shard=k/n` passthrough. The passthrough behaves exactly as `ci.yml`'s own measured comment says (it folds into every hash in the run); `--only` is the flag that drops the `build` / `^build` hashes out of the task hash.

The blast radius is not cli: it is **every package the partitioner slices, on every PR**. `--only` was introduced deliberately (#16395) to stop the slice leg re-hashing and rebuilding the whole `^build` closure under the passthrough, and the step above it does build that closure with no passthrough — so the dist on disk is fresh. That guard was written against a *missing* dist (「fails LOUDLY … never as a silent green」). It does not address a *stale cached test result*, which is what happens here: the job pays for the rebuild and then replays the test that the rebuild was supposed to re-validate.

### 4. The affected-set readings (the card's probe on the graph half) — all pinned, with the null control

Same worktree, turbo 2.10.10. Each reading states its base, per the instrument discipline the card paid for.

| reading | base | result |
|---|---|---|
| ⭐ null control — clean tree | `TURBO_SCM_BASE=HEAD` | `0 no packages` |
| clean tree, **unpinned** | (none) | `81 packages` — today's entire workspace |
| only `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` | `TURBO_SCM_BASE=HEAD` | `76 packages`, `@objectstack/cli` present |
| only `packages/types/src/env.ts` | `TURBO_SCM_BASE=HEAD` | `68 packages`, `@objectstack/cli` present |
| only `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts.md` | `TURBO_SCM_BASE=HEAD` | `76 packages`, `@objectstack/cli` present |

The card's `0 / 76 / 68` reproduce exactly. The unpinned null case reads **81** here, not 76 — because the unpinned reading is simply "every package in the workspace", and the workspace has grown from 76 to 81 since the card was filed. That makes the card's instrument warning sharper, not weaker: the unpinned number is the workspace size on the day, and it coincided with the affected-set size the original dev reported.

And the run's own affected set did include cli: `Test Core (5/6)` reported `check-test-completeness: OK (11 of 11 scheduled package(s) reported, 0 had nothing to run, 0 never reached; …)`, with the cli slice among them.

### 5. The `restore-keys` (the card's probe 1) — what a fallback hit restores

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` at the run's head `c7ae2c1026`, `Restore Turbo cache` (`actions/cache/restore@v6`, `path: .turbo/cache`):

- primary key: `OS-turbo-JOB-SHARD-REFNAME-SHA`
- restore-keys, in order: `OS-turbo-JOB-SHARD-REFNAME-` → across **commits** of the same ref; `OS-turbo-JOB-SHARD-` → across **branches**; `OS-turbo-JOB-` → across **branches and shards**.

A fallback hit restores turbo's local content-addressed cache directory: the task archives and the stored task logs, keyed by task hash. Because the save step is `if: always() && github.event_name == 'push'`, the entries in it can only have been produced by `main` push runs. So a PR job is handed a bag of results computed on `main`, and turbo replays any of them whose hash matches — which is correct as long as the hash is complete, and is exactly what §3 shows it is not under `--only`. There is no remote cache in play: no `TURBO_TOKEN` / `TURBO_API` / remote-cache configuration exists in the workflow or the repo (the same grep does find `TURBO_FORCE` and `TURBO_SCM_BASE`, so the reading is not a false zero).

### 6. NOT MEASURED, and why — ⛔ none of these is "not there"

- **The per-task cache record from that run** (`cache.status`, the matched hash). The job uploads `.turbo/runs` as `test-core-run-summary-5-of-6`, but that artifact carries `retention-days: 1` and the REST artifacts API reports `expired: true` (`expires_at: 2026-09-14T08:21:09Z`). Artifact download is separately blocked: the proxy denies CONNECT to `productionresultssa4.blob.core.windows.net`. The surviving `test-core-timing-table` artifact (expires 2026-09-27) is the same table already read out of the job log.
- **The `Restore Turbo cache` step's own "Cache restored from key …" line**, which would name which of the three restore-keys hit. It sits near the head of the job log and the available channel (`get_job_logs`) only tails. Control that the channel does surface such lines: the post-job `Cache hit occurred on the primary key Linux-pnpm-store-v3-…, not saving cache` line appears in the same tails.
- **Byte-level identification of the seeding cache entry.** Run `34745708702` is identified by chronology (only main push run whose `Test Core (5/6)` window contains `07:51:20`) and by the save condition, not by reading the entry.

What would settle those, if the PM wants it settled before a fix: raise `test-core-run-summary-*` retention, or have the slice leg print its plan hash, and re-read within retention on the next spec-touching PR. Nothing in §2/§3 depends on it.

### 7. Scope

⛔ No edit, no PR, no label. #10032 (a task that RAN and captured no output) was not touched — it stays a different object from this one: here the task did not run. #18236 / PR #18667 were not re-litigated; the bare-specifier premise stays falsified and is not load-bearing for anything above.
